review_note: Pinned lemma 6317 assumes Noetherian I-adically complete R and arbitrary index set A, and asserts UNIVERSAL injectivity of the canonical map from the I-adic completion of the direct sum R^(A) into the full product R^A. The preparation retains both the completed domain and stronger universally injective qualifier.
statement:
Let $R$ be a ring.
Let $I \subset R$ be an ideal.
Let $A$ be a set.
Assume $R$ is Noetherian and complete with respect to $I$. There is a
canonical map
$$
\left(\bigoplus\nolimits_{\alpha \in A} R\right)^\wedge
\longrightarrow
\prod\nolimits_{\alpha \in A} R
$$
from the $I$-adic completion of the direct sum into the product
which is universally injective.

\label{lemma-ui-completion-direct-sum-into-product}

review_note: Pinned safe lemma 6449–6463 states strict pro-zero for Tor_p(M,A/I^n) when A Noetherian and M finite: for EVERY p>0 there is c>0 with transition to n−c zero for ALL n≥c. The preparation retains quantifier order and the strict c independent of n.
statement:
Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring. Let $I$ be an ideal of $A$.
Let $M$ be a finite $A$-module. For every $p > 0$ there exists a $c > 0$
such that $\text{Tor}_p^A(M, A/I^n) \to \text{Tor}_p^A(M, A/I^{n - c})$
is zero for all $n \geq c$.

review_note: Pinned lemma 6474 uses an inverse system M_n of A-modules with each M_n flat over A/I^n and each transition M_(n+1)→M_n surjective, for A Noetherian. It concludes the inverse limit flat over A and commutation with tensor by EVERY finite A-module Q. The draft keeps both results.
statement:
Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring. Let $I$ be an ideal of $A$. Let
$(M_n)$ be an inverse system of $A$-modules such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $M_n$ is a flat $A/I^n$-module,
\item $M_{n + 1} \to M_n$ is surjective.
\end{enumerate}
Then $M = \lim M_n$ is a flat $A$-module and
$Q \otimes_A M = \lim Q \otimes_A M_n$ for every finite $A$-module $Q$.
conclusions:
$M = \lim M_n$ is a flat $A$-module and
$Q \otimes_A M = \lim Q \otimes_A M_n$ for every finite $A$-module $Q$.

review_note: Pinned lemma 6526 assumes I finitely generated, R/I Noetherian, M/IM flat over R/I, Tor_1^R(M,R/I)=0, and concludes both I-adic completion R^ is Noetherian and M^ flat over R^. All four premises and both independent conclusions are retained.
statement:
Let $R$ be a ring. Let $I \subset R$ be an ideal. Let $M$ be
an $R$-module. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $I$ is finitely generated,
\item $R/I$ is Noetherian,
\item $M/IM$ is flat over $R/I$,
\item $\text{Tor}_1^R(M, R/I) = 0$.
\end{enumerate}
Then the $I$-adic completion $R^\wedge$
is a Noetherian ring and $M^\wedge$ is flat over $R^\wedge$.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-flat-after-completion}
Let $R$ be a ring. Let $I \subset R$ be an ideal. Let $M$ be
an $R$-module. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $I$ is finitely generated,
\item $R/I$ is Noetherian,
\item $M/IM$ is flat over $R/I$,
\item $\text{Tor}_1^R(M, R/I) = 0$.
\end{enumerate}
Then the $I$-adic completion $R^\wedge$
is a Noetherian ring and $M^\wedge$ is flat over $R^\wedge$.
